questions.title: Mode of milk secretion
questions.question: The mode of secretion of milk from the cells of the mammary gland is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Merocrine (exocytosis) accounts for the protein fraction of milk only, so "merocrine" alone is incomplete.
explanations.B: Correct. Milk is secreted by two modes at once. The protein component (casein, lactalbumin) leaves the alveolar cell by MEROCRINE exocytosis, whereas the fat (lipid droplets) is released by the APOCRINE mode, pinching off with a thin envelope of apical cytoplasm and membrane. So the lactating mammary gland uses a combined merocrine-plus-apocrine secretion.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Apocrine covers only the lipid fraction; the proteins are released by merocrine exocytosis, so apocrine alone is incomplete.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Holocrine secretion (whole-cell disintegration, as in sebaceous glands) does not occur in the mammary gland.

questions.learning_objective: State that the mammary gland secretes milk by a combined merocrine (protein) and apocrine (fat) mode.

questions.title: Immunoglobulin of mammary secretion
questions.question: Which type of immunoglobulin is present in the mammary secretion?

explanations.A: Incorrect. IgM is not the immunoglobulin transferred into milk in significant amount.
explanations.B: Correct. The dominant immunoglobulin of colostrum and milk is secretory IgA. Plasma cells in the connective tissue between the alveoli produce dimeric IgA, which the alveolar cells take up and secrete into the milk with a secretory component. This passive immunity protects the newborn's gut.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Some IgG crosses the placenta before birth, but the immunoglobulin characteristic of the mammary secretion is IgA.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IgD has no role in the mammary secretion.

questions.learning_objective: Identify secretory IgA as the immunoglobulin of the mammary secretion.

questions.title: Source of the mammary immunoglobulin
questions.question: The immunoglobulin in the mammary secretion is secreted by:

options.B: Plasma cells in the tissue between the alveoli

explanations.A: Incorrect. The alveolar cells transport and release the IgA into the milk (adding the secretory component), but they do not synthesise the antibody itself.
explanations.B: Correct. The IgA of milk is synthesised by PLASMA CELLS lying in the loose connective tissue between the alveoli. Their dimeric IgA is then taken up at the base of the alveolar cell, coupled to a secretory component and released into the lumen, so the ultimate source of the antibody is the interstitial plasma cell.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Myoepithelial cells are contractile cells that eject milk; they do not make immunoglobulin.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Duct cells convey milk and do not synthesise the immunoglobulin.

questions.learning_objective: State that the IgA of milk is made by plasma cells in the interalveolar connective tissue.

questions.title: Duct draining a mammary lobe
questions.question: Each lobe in the mammary gland is drained by a duct called:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Interlobular ducts run between the lobules within a lobe; they are not the duct of a whole lobe.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The glands (and tubercles) of Montgomery are sebaceous glands of the areola, not the drainage duct of a mammary lobe.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Interlobar duct" is not the standard name for the main duct of a lobe.
explanations.D: Correct. The mammary gland has 15-20 lobes, and each lobe is drained by a single LACTIFEROUS DUCT that opens on the nipple. Near the nipple each lactiferous duct widens into a lactiferous sinus that stores milk between feeds.

questions.learning_objective: State that each mammary lobe is drained by a lactiferous duct opening on the nipple.

questions.title: Layers of the placental barrier
questions.question: The placental barrier is formed of all the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Fenestrated endothelium of the fetal blood vessels

explanations.A: Correct. The endothelium of the fetal villous capillary is a CONTINUOUS (non-fenestrated) endothelium, not a fenestrated one, so "fenestrated endothelium" is the false statement and the required exception. The layers of the placental barrier are the syncytiotrophoblast (and, early on, the cytotrophoblast), the trophoblastic basal lamina, the villous connective tissue, and the fetal capillary endothelium with its basement membrane.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The basement membrane of the fetal capillary endothelium is a genuine layer of the barrier.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The syncytiotrophoblast is the outermost, essential layer of the placental barrier.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The fetal (villous) connective tissue is a true intervening layer of the barrier.

questions.learning_objective: List the layers of the placental barrier and recognise that the fetal capillary endothelium is continuous, not fenestrated.

questions.title: The placental barrier in late pregnancy
questions.question: In the late months of pregnancy, all the following are components of the placental barrier EXCEPT:

options.A: The endothelium of the fetal capillary
options.B: The basal lamina of the trophoblast

explanations.A: Incorrect. The fetal capillary endothelium remains a layer of the barrier throughout pregnancy.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The trophoblastic basal lamina persists as a barrier layer in late pregnancy.
explanations.C: Correct. As pregnancy advances the cytotrophoblast (Langhans layer) becomes discontinuous and largely disappears, so by the late months it is no longer a component of the thinned placental barrier. The remaining layers are the syncytiotrophoblast, its basal lamina, thin villous connective tissue and the fetal capillary endothelium, which shortens the diffusion distance and increases exchange near term.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The syncytiotrophoblast is retained as the outer layer of the barrier at all stages.

questions.learning_objective: State that the cytotrophoblast is lost from the placental barrier in late pregnancy.

questions.title: Maternal part of the placenta
questions.question: The maternal part of the placenta is the:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The decidua parietalis lines the rest of the uterine cavity away from the implantation site and does not form the placenta.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The chorion (chorion frondosum) is the FETAL part of the placenta, not the maternal part.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The decidua capsularis covers the conceptus toward the uterine lumen and does not form the placenta.
explanations.D: Correct. The maternal part of the placenta is the decidua basalis — the endometrium underlying the implantation site, into which the chorionic villi are anchored and where the intervillous space forms. The fetal part is the chorion frondosum, and the two interlock to form the definitive placenta.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the decidua basalis as the maternal part of the placenta.

questions.title: Fetal part of the placenta
questions.question: The fetal part of the placenta is called:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The fibrinoid (Nitabuch/Rohr) material is a deposit at the maternal-fetal junction, not the fetal part of the placenta.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cooper's ligaments are suspensory ligaments of the breast, unrelated to the placenta.
explanations.C: Correct. The fetal part of the placenta is the chorion — specifically the chorion frondosum, the villous chorion whose branching chorionic villi project into the intervillous space. It interlocks with the maternal decidua basalis to form the definitive placenta.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The decidua capsularis is maternal endometrium covering the conceptus, not the fetal part of the placenta.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the chorion (frondosum) as the fetal part of the placenta.

questions.title: Regions of the decidua
questions.question: All the following are regions of the decidua EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The decidua parietalis is the part lining the rest of the uterine cavity, a genuine region of the decidua.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The decidua basalis lies deep to the implantation site and forms the maternal placenta, a true region.
explanations.C: Correct. The pregnant endometrium (decidua) is divided into three regions — basalis (under the conceptus), capsularis (over the conceptus toward the lumen) and parietalis (lining the rest of the cavity). There is no "decidua vaginalis"; the decidua is a uterine, not a vaginal, structure, so this is the required exception.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The decidua capsularis is the thin part covering the conceptus toward the uterine lumen, a true region of the decidua.

questions.learning_objective: Name the three regions of the decidua (basalis, capsularis, parietalis) and exclude a "decidua vaginalis".

questions.title: Features of syncytiotrophoblast
questions.question: Syncytiotrophoblasts are characterised by all the following EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct. The syncytiotrophoblast is an active steroid- and peptide-secreting layer. Because it synthesises progesterone and oestrogens from cholesterol, it is RICH in lipid droplets and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, not devoid of them. So "devoid of lipid droplets" is the false statement and the required exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The syncytiotrophoblast secretes human chorionic gonadotropin (as well as human placental lactogen, progesterone and oestrogens), so this is true.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The syncytiotrophoblast is a non-mitotic syncytium; it grows only by fusion of underlying cytotrophoblast cells, so "non-mitotic" is a true feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Its apical surface bears abundant microvilli (a brush border) facing the maternal blood, increasing the exchange surface, so this is true.

questions.learning_objective: State that the syncytiotrophoblast is a non-mitotic, microvillous, hormone-secreting layer rich in lipid droplets.

questions.title: Ultrastructure of the theca interna
questions.question: The differentiated theca-interna cells have the ultrastructural characteristics of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ion-transporting cells have basal membrane infoldings with mitochondria; that is not the theca-interna pattern.
explanations.B: Correct. The differentiated theca-interna cells acquire the ultrastructure of STEROID-SECRETING cells — abundant smooth endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria with tubular cristae and lipid droplets. Under LH they convert cholesterol to androgens, which the neighbouring granulosa cells aromatise to oestrogen (the two-cell mechanism).
explanations.C: Incorrect. Protein-secreting cells are dominated by rough ER and basophilia, which is not the theca-interna phenotype.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mucous-secreting cells contain apical mucin granules, unlike the steroid-type theca interna.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the theca-interna cell as a steroid-secreting cell (smooth ER, tubular-cristae mitochondria, lipid).

questions.title: The germinal epithelium of the ovary
questions.question: The germinal epithelium of the ovary is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The surface of the ovary is a single layer, not a stratified columnar epithelium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. It is not pseudostratified columnar; the ovarian surface cells form one simple layer.
explanations.C: Correct. The free surface of the ovary is covered by a simple cuboidal (sometimes low columnar) epithelium — the so-called germinal epithelium, continuous with the peritoneal mesothelium. The name is a historical misnomer: it does NOT give rise to the germ cells; it merely covers the tunica albuginea of the ovary.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Transitional epithelium lines the urinary tract, not the ovarian surface.

questions.learning_objective: State that the ovarian germinal epithelium is a simple cuboidal surface epithelium (a misnomer).

questions.title: Location of the corpus luteum
questions.question: The corpus luteum is characterised by all the following EXCEPT:

options.B: Present in the medulla of the ovary

explanations.A: Incorrect. The corpus luteum secretes both progesterone (granulosa lutein cells) and oestrogen (theca lutein cells), so this is true.
explanations.B: Correct. The corpus luteum forms from the ruptured follicle in the ovarian CORTEX, where all the follicles and their derivatives lie; the medulla holds only vessels, nerves and loose connective tissue. So "present in the medulla" is false and is the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The corpus luteum is a temporary endocrine gland that regresses (to a corpus albicans) if pregnancy does not occur, so this is true.
explanations.D: Incorrect. After ovulation the oocyte has been shed, so the corpus luteum contains no oocyte — a true feature.

questions.learning_objective: State that the corpus luteum (like the follicles) lies in the ovarian cortex, not the medulla.

questions.title: What leaves the ovary at ovulation
questions.question: All the following leave the ovary after ovulation EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The corona radiata — the innermost granulosa cells clinging to the zona pellucida — is shed with the oocyte at ovulation.
explanations.B: Correct. At ovulation the secondary oocyte is extruded together with its zona pellucida, corona radiata and surrounding cumulus cells. The THECA INTERNA stays behind in the ovarian wall, where (with the granulosa) it luteinises to form the corpus luteum. So the theca interna is the structure that does NOT leave the ovary and is the required exception.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The cumulus oophorus cells that detach with the oocyte are carried out at ovulation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The secondary oocyte is the cell that is released at ovulation.

questions.learning_objective: State that the oocyte, corona radiata and cumulus are extruded at ovulation while the theca interna is retained (to form the corpus luteum).

questions.title: Glands of the secretory endometrium
questions.question: All the following are true for the endometrium in the secretory phase EXCEPT:

options.C: Mitosis is rare in its cells

explanations.A: Correct. In the secretory (luteal) phase under progesterone the endometrial glands become long, tortuous and sacculated (a corkscrew/saw-tooth outline), NOT straight tubules. Straight, simple tubular glands belong to the early proliferative phase, so "straight tubules" is the false statement and the required exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The endometrium reaches its maximum thickness in the secretory phase, so this is true.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Progesterone suppresses proliferation, so mitoses are rare in the secretory phase — a true feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Secretory-phase gland cells accumulate glycogen (basal then luminal secretion), which is true.

questions.learning_objective: State that secretory-phase endometrial glands are coiled and sacculated, not straight tubules.

questions.title: Epithelium of the vagina
questions.question: All the following are true about the vagina EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Correct. The vagina is lined by a thick, stratified squamous NON-keratinised epithelium rich in glycogen, not by transitional epithelium (which lines the urinary tract). So "its epithelium is transitional" is false and is the required exception.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The vagina has no serous glands of its own; this is a true feature.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The vaginal wall (lamina propria) is highly vascular, which is true and contributes to its lubricating transudate.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The vagina is glandless — it has no mucous glands and is lubricated by cervical mucus and vascular transudate, so this is true.

questions.learning_objective: State that the vagina is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium (not transitional).
